Laura / Sam — quick technical note. There are two likely causes: the forwarder stripped the organizer header or the invite was created in a secondary calendar that sets private ACLs. If the organizer is an external alias that forwarded the invite, GCal can block rendering for downstream domains.

We have two actionable paths:
- Organizer transfer / claim: we attempt a host claim flow. That sometimes works (we PATCH the event organizer via API) but can be blocked by domain policies; it's worth trying but not guaranteed.
- Replace the event: create a new event from our domain (we send an invite with both Meet and Zoom links). That is the most robust for cross-tenant reliability.

If we replace the event, steps I'll take: create new event on laura@redwood.com, include Priya and Sam as required, include it-admin as optional, add a one-line note explaining migration, and attach a regenerated .ics (see attached redwood-temp-zoom.ics). I'll also include a short note for their IT about why the migration was necessary so it doesn't look suspicious.

I'll proceed with replacement unless Sam asks for organizer-claim attempt. Ben
